decisions.reason: As a large established machinery firm in a growing industry, we would keep this coolant pressure booster system because it fits the core portfolio, complements existing systems, and there is no clear evidence yet that its early results fall below aspiration levels enough to justify redeploying resources.

We would keep the coolant cleaning centrifuge because it builds directly on our established coolant-management capabilities and, under uncertainty after a recent launch, organisational slack supports continued market presence while learning accumulates.

We would keep the coolant nozzles because they are closely tied to the existing offer, likely support cross-selling into installed systems, and there is no indication of performance so poor relative to aspirations that problemistic search should replace them.

We would keep the scraper belt chip conveyor because it is close to the firm’s established automation and conveying business, and a broad-line German machinery producer would usually tolerate initial uncertainty for such a strategically adjacent product.

We would keep the magnetic belt chip conveyor because it extends an existing product family in a growing market and there is no observed shortfall versus aspiration levels strong enough to warrant dropping it after only a short time on the market.

We would keep the hinged belt chip conveyor because it is adjacent to the established chip-handling range, benefits from shared engineering and service resources, and a large firm would typically continue it until clearer evidence of underperformance emerges.
